title: fix(plugin-dashboard,cli): converge the bare `dashboard` key on `plugin-dashboard`, retire `view:dashboard` with a by-name tombstone
body:
Fixes #9533

Ruled shape, executed: director seat summon #24, batch #152 item 5, **letter 1**, maintainer 「其他同意」 2026-09-18 (issue comment 5724939774). Routes 2 and 3 were rejected on the record and are not reopened here.

## The reproduction came first, and it confirmed the card

The card and the ruling both required the never-cleared stub to be reproduced against a real `Registry` before acting, because it had been read off `Registry.register`'s clearing lines rather than executed. It was, on a fresh `Registry` fed this package's REAL declared metadata read back out of the registry:

```text
=== fresh Registry, stub then eager (what the console does) ===
  after stub : hasLazy('dashboard','plugin-dashboard') = true
  after stub : getMeta('dashboard')?.namespace = "plugin-dashboard"
  after load : hasLazy('dashboard','plugin-dashboard') = true   <-- THE CLAIM
  after load : getMeta('dashboard')?.namespace = "view"
  after load : get('dashboard','plugin-dashboard') = undefined
=== collision warnings seen ===
  0
```

Both consequences reproduce. The stub is never cleared (`register()` clears the stub of the type IT registers, and that type was `view:dashboard`), the whitelisted key resolves to `undefined` forever, and the bare key's declared namespace flips mid-sequence. The zero collision warnings are the triage seat's point measured: this shape came in through `registerLazy`, which takes the same fallback branch with no collision check at all.

Nothing falsified the ruling.

## What letter 1 required, and where each clause landed

| clause | where |
| --- | --- |
| package registers `plugin-dashboard:dashboard`; the `view` namespace registration goes | `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/index.tsx` |
| authored `view:dashboard` refused BY NAME with a tombstone pointing at `plugin-dashboard:dashboard` | `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/retired-node-types.tsx`, registered last with `skipFallback: true` |
| `content/docs/plugins/plugin-dashboard.mdx` row regenerates | that file, plus the package README's twin table |
| CLI whitelist regenerates | `packages/cli/src/utils/known-schema-types.ts`, one line: `view:dashboard` leaves |
| `check-registry-bare-name-collisions.mjs`'s row for this pair goes | the shrink-only ledger is now **empty** |
| ownership pinned in BOTH orders, `hasLazy` false after load | `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/__tests__/dashboardBareKeyOwnership.test.tsx` |

The ledger row was **deleted, not reworded** — the gate now prints `0 contested; ledger holds 0`.

## Why the tombstone spelling is withheld from the key universe

A literal `register('dashboard', Tombstone, { namespace: 'view' })` would have put `view:dashboard` straight back into `deriveRegistryKeys`' universe and therefore back into `KNOWN_SCHEMA_TYPES` — and objectui#8760 graded exactly that as the wrong side of the line: *"an unknown key is refused loudly at authoring time; a registered-but-unfulfilled key passes every check, is taught by the documentation, and fails only at render in front of a user."* Blessing the retired spelling in the CLI would have rebuilt the defect this card removes, one spelling over.

So the tombstone registrar is collection-keyed and declared `excluded` in `INDIRECT_REGISTRATIONS`, the same disposition `RETIRED_FIELD_TYPES`' tombstones already take (objectui#9717 holds the open question; both are answered the same way so they cannot drift apart). Net effect: the runtime points the author at the replacement, and `objectui check` names the retired spelling instead of blessing it.

## The pin, and the reverse verification that proves it can fail

Both ablation legs ran against the COMMITTED fix, each with an on-disk mutation proof and a restore proven by `git diff HEAD` being empty:

- **Leg 1 — namespace back to `view`** (occurrences of the new spelling 8 to 7, blob `cf38965` to `ee4c498`): the pin goes **7 of 10 red**; `check:registry-bare-names` exits 1 and reprints the card's own finding verbatim, naming all three claimants; `regenerate-known-schema-types.mjs --check` exits 1.
- **Leg 2 — tombstone registrar deleted** (registrar call 1 to 0, blob `cf38965` to `36f5964`): **5 of 10 red**, including `view:dashboard` resolves to the TOMBSTONE, not to the renderer and renders the tombstone, carrying the migration text the table declares.

Leg 2 exists because the refusal is the assertion most easily faked. The pin asserts the refusal **and** the tombstone's own text (read from the table the component reads, never restated), the `role="alert"` element, the `data-retired-node-type` attribute and the `console.error` carrying the same string — plus a control that bare `dashboard` and `plugin-dashboard:dashboard` still paint the real grid, so "nothing rendered" cannot pass for a refusal.

## Clause-②: yes — and what the mechanical floor does NOT prove

Declared by the ruling: the published full name moves. The shape is unusual and worth stating so it does not confuse a reviewer's measurement — **the accept set narrows** (an authored `view:dashboard` stops resolving) and the clause is `yes` anyway, on the published-name move rather than on a widened surface.

⇒ the `^\+export` floor is useless here **in both directions**. Counted against this branch's merge-base `42234b1a`: it adds **5** `^\+export` lines — four in the new `retired-node-types.tsx` (`RETIRED_DASHBOARD_NODE_TYPES`, `reportRetiredDashboardNodeType`, `resetRetiredDashboardNodeTypeReports`, `RetiredDashboardNodeTombstone`) and one `export { … } from './retired-node-types'` block in `index.tsx`. ⚠️ **An earlier revision of this paragraph said 2, and named only two of the symbols — that was wrong**; the at-tier contract review measured the floor at 5 off the head diff, and re-measuring it here reproduces 5 (same number at `588e45950f` and at head). That count proves neither half of the clause. It does not prove `yes`, because those five lines are a NEW surface rather than the moved published name the clause is actually about — and to be exact about what kind of surface: the four symbols are **published**, not internal. `src/index.tsx` is the file this package's `exports["."]` publishes, so anything that resolves `@object-ui/plugin-dashboard` can import them, and dropping one later is a breaking change like any other export. (They are declared in the changeset as of `96b6ee2820`.) It could not have proven `no` either, because the thing that moved — the string `plugin-dashboard:dashboard` replacing `view:dashboard` inside a `register(...)` call — adds no export line at all and would score 0 on a floor that only counts them. The clause rests on the registry key, which is a runtime string, and the instrument that re-derives it is `dashboardBareKeyOwnership.test.tsx` plus the regenerated whitelist, not a diff-line count.

Changeset marked `minor` per AGENTS.md's 版本号策略 (objectui's own breaking changes take `minor`, with the breaking semantics written out), naming the tombstone under 「Breaking for authored metadata」.

## Verification

Ordinary-direction result throughout; nothing reversed or fanned out.

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-dashboard/ packages/cli/ packages/app-shell/src/__tests__/widget-dom-leak-sweep.test.tsx` plus the four affected `scripts/__tests__/` files — **143 files, 1806 tests, all passing** after the one collateral repair below (first run caught it: 1 failed / 1805 passed).
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-dashboard type-check`, `pnpm --filter @object-ui/cli type-check`, `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` in `@object-ui/app-shell` — all exit 0, each on a tree whose dependency closure was built first (an unbuilt closure answers `TS2307` for every workspace import, which is a missing prerequisite and not a verdict).
- Gates exit 0: `check:registry-bare-names`, `check:doc-types`, `check:side-effects-array`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:changeset-presence`, `check:changeset-no-major`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:entry-guard`, `check:prompt-keys`, `check:doc-fences`, `check:doc-example-ids`, `check:component-surface-parity`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`.

**Collateral repair, in scope because this branch caused it.** `dashboardAuthoredInputs.test.tsx` looked the `inputs` list up under the `view` namespace. That key now answers the tombstone, which publishes no `inputs` at all — so the objectui#5742 "publishes neither" half would have read an empty list and passed while measuring nothing. Its own `label` / `widgets` controls caught it; the row moved to `plugin-dashboard` rather than being dropped.

**Other call sites updated to the new full type**: `DashboardRenderer.domProps.test.tsx` (the canary node and its `data-obj-type` assertion), `widget-dom-leak-sweep.test.tsx` (the sweep target moved under the `plugin-dashboard:` prefix case; its `OWNED_VIEW_ALIASES` entry is now empty, with the reason written down — `view:dashboard` is still a registered key but what answers it destructures and spreads nothing, so there is no pass-through surface for that sweep to measure), and the doc-gate test's table-row pin.

## Not built here, reported instead

- `Registry.registerLazy` has **no collision check** while `Registry.register` warns, and this shape came in through that unguarded door. True, and a **different card** — the dispatch is explicit that it is reported and not built.
- `packages/types` was deliberately not touched; the tombstone needed nothing there.

## Update after `main` was merged in

Re-run at `ecf5fc69f`: **143 test files, 1806 tests, 0 failures**, and `check:registry-bare-names`, `check:doc-types`, `check:side-effects-array`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:changeset-presence`, `check:new-line-citations` and `regenerate-known-schema-types.mjs --check` all exit 0 on that same tree.

⚠️ **`ecf5fc69f` is NOT this PR's head, and every figure under Verification above is measured on `ecf5fc69f` and on nothing later.** An earlier revision of this paragraph called it "final head … the sha every count in Verification above is measured on"; the first half of that has been false since the branch moved. It moved twice: `588e45950f` (the one-line unused-`eslint-disable` deletion described below, plus a merge of `main`) and then `96b6ee2820` (the three items the at-tier contract review listed as owed before merge — the corrected `excluded` sentence in `check-doc-component-types.mjs`, the changeset's two missing declarations, and this body). The 143/1806 figures were **not** re-measured at either, and this body does not claim they were. What stands for head is CI, plus the gates re-run per commit: at `96b6ee2820`, `check:doc-types`, `check:registry-bare-names`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:changeset-presence`, `check:changeset-no-major`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:doc-fences`, `check:doc-example-ids`, `check:comment-mask-corpus`, `check:shell-escape-residue`, `check:unreferenced-sources` and `regenerate-known-schema-types.mjs --check` each exit 0, `pnpm exec eslint scripts/check-doc-component-types.mjs --format json` judges 1 file with 0 errors and 0 warnings, and `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/check-doc-component-types.test.ts scripts/__tests__/known-schema-types-derivation-5115.test.ts packages/cli/src/__tests__/retired-view-dashboard-key-9533.test.ts` reports 3 files / 136 tests passed. The `excluded` correction was measured before it was written: dropping that line yields `stale-indirect-registration` (both commands exit 1, nothing written), not the re-admission the sentence used to claim.

Two gates that need a BUILT tree were also run once the closures were built: `check:sdui-registration-pins` exits 0 (16 promised registrations present across 2309 weighed chunks, the 3 ruled controls in the derived set) and `check:eager-closure` exits 0, both against a freshly built `apps/console`. `check:doc-snippets`, `check:doc-examples` and `check:readme-exports` remain **NOT MEASURED**: each exits on a missing prerequisite (7 packages outside the closures this branch needed are still unbuilt), and none of their unjudgeable entries names a file this branch edits.

⚠️ **Corrected by the claiming seat after CI went red — the reading this paragraph used to carry could not have failed.** An earlier revision reported `pnpm exec eslint . --no-inline-config --format json` judging **5079 files** with **0 errors**. That reading was blind to the very error class that turned CI red: `--no-inline-config` makes eslint skip inline configuration comments entirely, so an **unused** `eslint-disable` directive cannot be reported at all. The flag did not add noise — it removed a rule's ability to fire — and it is the sister repository's spelling; this repo's `lint` script takes no flags. CI's `Lint` job failed on exactly that: one error, `Unused eslint-disable directive (no problems were reported from 'no-console')` at `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/retired-node-types.tsx:72`. The directive is removed — one deletion, nothing else; no `console` call added back and no flag added anywhere.

**The honest reading, taken with the instrument CI actually runs:** `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-dashboard lint` exits **0** with `501 problems (0 errors, 501 warnings)` — CI's 502 minus the one error — and the full `pnpm lint` (`turbo run lint`, 47 tasks) exits **0**, every package's summary line reading `0 errors`, `//:lint:root` included, with `Unused eslint-disable` appearing nowhere in the tree. The warning split below stands, measured per file at base versus head: **17 pre-existing, 5 new**, every new one `react-refresh/only-export-components` — 2 from `index.tsx`'s new re-export block and 3 from `retired-node-types.tsx`, which exports a component beside its table exactly as `@object-ui/fields` does for `RetiredFieldTombstone`. No package's `lint` script sets `--max-warnings`.

**One repair this branch owed itself.** `check-doc-component-types.mjs`'s header ran its objectui#5106 namespace-blindness example over the literal pair `view:dashboard` / `plugin-dashboard:dashboard` and told the reader to flip `namespace: 'view'` on the dashboard registration. This branch made that false — there is no `namespace: 'view'` on that registration any more — so the example is re-pointed with a note saying what moved. Not opportunistic tidying: a claim this diff falsified, in a file this diff already edits.

Seat session, in prose so it survives an edit: `session_012EpHzwH4wTy5sd7ibkD2yq`.

`needs:contract-review` is hung on **both** carriers — the claiming seat hung the PR-side half after this PR was opened, since that half is the PM's — and `check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 9803` now exits **0**. Arranging the clause-② review belongs to the claiming seat; ⛔ this branch does not wait on it.
